title: 1987 AHSME Problem 9
statement: The first four terms of an arithmetic sequence are \(a,\) \(x,\) \(b,\) \(2x.\) The ratio of \(a\) to \(b\) is

solutions.text:
Let the common difference be \(d.\) Then \(x=a+d,\ b=a+2d,\) and \(2x=a+3d.\) Thus \[ 2(a+d)=a+3d, \] so \(a=d\) and \(b=3d.\) Therefore \(\frac{a}{b}=\frac{1}{3}.\)

Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: Write all four terms using \(a\) and a common difference
Use the equation relating the second term \(x\) to the fourth term \(2x\)
